questions.stem: For the function shown in the graph, complete the table by stating whether the first derivative \( y' \) and the second derivative \( y'' \) are positive, negative, or zero at each of the labeled points A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I.

steps.explain: Point A is a local minimum: tangent is horizontal (\( y' = 0 \)) and curve is concave up (\( y'' > 0 \)).
Point B is on the rising section where concavity changes from up to down: rising (\( y' > 0 \)) and point of inflection (\( y'' = 0 \)).
Point C is a local maximum: tangent is horizontal (\( y' = 0 \)) and curve is concave down (\( y'' < 0 \)).
Point D is on the falling section where concavity changes from down to up: falling (\( y' < 0 \)) and point of inflection (\( y'' = 0 \)).
Points E and F are on the falling section after the inflection point: falling (\( y' < 0 \)) and concave up (\( y'' > 0 \)).
Point G is a local minimum: tangent is horizontal (\( y' = 0 \)) and curve is concave up (\( y'' > 0 \)).
Points H and I are on the rising section where the curve continues to bend upwards: rising (\( y' > 0 \)) and concave up (\( y'' > 0 \)).

parts.stem: Evaluate \( f''(0) \) and \( g''(0) \). Can you determine the nature of the stationary points at \( x=0 \) from this calculation?
options: \( f''(0) = 0 \) and \( g''(0) = 1 \). No, the test is inconclusive.
\( f''(0) = 0 \) and \( g''(0) = 0 \). Yes, this means both are inflection points.
\( f''(0) = 0 \) and \( g''(0) = 0 \). Yes, this means both are minimum points.
\( f''(0) = 0 \) and \( g''(0) = 0 \). No, the second derivative test is inconclusive.

steps.explain: Substitute \( x = 0 \) into \( f''(x) \) and \( g''(x) \).
Interpret the result.
steps.work: \text{When the second derivative is exactly 0 at a stationary point, the test fails to classify it. We must use the first derivative test (slope table).}

parts.stem: Use the first derivative test to determine the nature of the stationary points at \( x=0 \) for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \).
options: \( f(x) \) has a horizontal point of inflection, \( g(x) \) has a maximum.
\( f(x) \) has a horizontal point of inflection, \( g(x) \) has a minimum.
\( f(x) \) has a minimum, \( g(x) \) has a minimum.
\( f(x) \) has a minimum, \( g(x) \) has a horizontal point of inflection.

steps.explain: Test the slope of \( f(x) \) on either side of \( x=0 \).
steps.work: \begin{aligned} f'(-1) &= 6(-1)^2 = 6 > 0 \, (\text{increasing}) \\ f'(1) &= 6(1)^2 = 6 > 0 \, (\text{increasing}) \end{aligned} \\ \text{Since the slope does not change sign, } f(x) \text{ has a horizontal point of inflection.}

steps.explain: Test the slope of \( g(x) \) on either side of \( x=0 \).
steps.work: \begin{aligned} g'(-1) &= 12(-1)^3 = -12 < 0 \, (\text{decreasing}) \\ g'(1) &= 12(1)^3 = 12 > 0 \, (\text{increasing}) \end{aligned} \\ \text{Since the slope changes from negative to positive, } g(x) \text{ has a minimum.}
